newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber down on strong yen, holidays.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber down on strong yen, holidays.

text.p: Trading in the Singapore rubber market closed weakly on Monday, dragged down by the firm yen and a string of Buddhist holidays in the main rubber-producing areas of Southeast Asia, dealers said.
"The holidays kept people out. The yen's rise against the (U.S.) dollar is also not good for the market," a trader said. "Trading today was very, very flat."
"The rubber market today is simply not as hot as the coffee market," a dealer said, refering to the meteoric rally in world coffee markets. "There are no strong features in the rubber trade."
Dealers said a Buddhist holiday which is being celebrated in Thailand on Tuesday, and in Singapore, Malaysia and Indonesia over the next two days will put a damper on trade.
"We have to see if people will roll over their positions or liquidate them this week," a dealer said.
Malaysian-origin SMR rubber was said to be enjoying a discount to the RSS3 rubber produced by Thailand after Bangkok raised its support price for the local rubber industry, but buying was very thin.
At 0945 GMT, October/December RSS3 was seen at 118.75 U.S. cents a kg from 118.50 cents. - Rene Pastor (65-8703305)
